guard: a source-checkout CLI refuses to write or GC the operator-global seed store; unknown identity is refused; only COTAL_ALLOW_CHECKOUT_SEED=1 is the deliberate opt-in
why: SIX MUTATIONS, one per independent promise. Every find window is a unique code-only span.
M1 deletes the write refusal. That restores #1215: a checkout stages a payload into the
operator-global store. The first cell that can notice is the staging refusal.
M2 deletes the GC refusal. A checkout can still be refused on write, so the suite has to reach
gcSeedStore with an unreferenced generation already on disk. The GC cell is the first red.
M3 lets an unknown writer through the assert. Classification still reports unknown; the unknown
identity staging cell is the first red. That is the fail-closed contract: no-data is not all-clear.
M4 classifies a repo-shaped bin/cotal-ai as released. The classification cell is first because it
M5 treats any truthy COTAL_ALLOW_CHECKOUT_SEED as the opt-in, so =0 writes. The non-1 cell is first.
M6 puts the opt-in back on the refusal line. Isolation is still named, so the cell that forbids
advertising the bypass is the first red.

mutations.name: a checkout can write the operator-global seed payload again (the write refusal is deleted)
mutations.replace:
if (!opts.force && existsSync(join(dest, "package.json"))) return dest;
  const src = shippedSourceDir(name);
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: checkout: staging an operator-global seed payload is refused
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: checkout: staging an operator-global seed payload is refused

mutations.name: a checkout can GC an unreferenced operator-global generation again (the GC refusal is deleted)
mutations.replace:
if (referenced) continue;
    rmSync(genDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: checkout: GC of an unreferenced operator-global generation is refused
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: checkout: GC of an unreferenced operator-global generation is refused

mutations.name: an unknown writer is treated as a released install at the assert, so no-data is all-clear
mutations.replace:
const kind = seedWriterKind();
  if (kind === "released" || kind === "unknown") return;
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: unknown identity: staging is refused rather than treated as a released install
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: unknown identity: staging is refused rather than treated as a released install

mutations.name: a repo-shaped bin/cotal-ai is classified as a released install
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: classification: a repo-shaped bin/cotal-ai is a checkout
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: classification: a repo-shaped bin/cotal-ai is a checkout

mutations.name: any truthy COTAL_ALLOW_CHECKOUT_SEED is treated as the deliberate opt-in
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: checkout: a non-1 COTAL_ALLOW_CHECKOUT_SEED is not an opt-in
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: checkout: a non-1 COTAL_ALLOW_CHECKOUT_SEED is not an opt-in

mutations.name: the checkout refusal advertises COTAL_ALLOW_CHECKOUT_SEED as the way out
mutations.find: `refusing to ${action} the operator-global seed store at ${seedStoreDir()} for generation ${generation} from ${origin} (${entry}) - this would migrate the machine-wide store and can take an installed cotal down. Isolate with XDG_CONFIG_HOME. COTAL_HOME does not relocate this store.`,
mutations.replace: `refusing to ${action} the operator-global seed store at ${seedStoreDir()} for generation ${generation} from ${origin} (${entry}) - this would migrate the machine-wide store and can take an installed cotal down. Isolate with XDG_CONFIG_HOME. COTAL_HOME does not relocate this store. Set COTAL_ALLOW_CHECKOUT_SEED=1 to write deliberately.`,
mutations.expectRed: ✗ FAIL: checkout: the refusal does not advertise COTAL_ALLOW_CHECKOUT_SEED
mutations.cell: ✗ FAIL: checkout: the refusal does not advertise COTAL_ALLOW_CHECKOUT_SEED
